case_analysis.apparent_benchmark_claim: A successful AppWorld record solved the stated task: befriend on Venmo anyone sent money to this month and unfriend everyone else.
case_analysis.actual_checked_outcome: Released success was `TestTracker.success` over five registered tests only: the end-state task answer had to match ground-truth `null`; `models.changed_model_names()` had to be exactly `{venmo.Friendship}` after the helper’s default ignores; added friendship `friend_id`s had to match `private_data.to_befriend_user_ids`; removed friendship `friend_id`s had to match `private_data.to_unfriend_user_ids`; and `models.changed_records("venmo.Friendship")` had to report zero updated records. The evaluator assigned `test.task_completed`, but that assignment was not itself a scored test.
case_analysis.target_construction_review: The target construction is explicit and coherent: `answer.json` fixes the answer target to `null`, and `private_data.json` fixes the exact add/remove friendship ID sets used by the evaluator.
case_analysis.evaluator_oracle_review: The evaluator is slightly weaker than a naive task-completion reading because only `with test(requirement)` blocks register tests. `test.task_completed = active_tasks[0].status == "success"` is computed but does not affect `passes`, `failures`, `num_tests`, or `success`.
case_analysis.reward_wiring_aggregation_review: There is no separate reward predicate. `evaluate_task` returns a `TestTracker`; `run_official_job` serializes that tracker; the campaign runner carries the worker summary; and the released label join reads `native_evaluator_output.json::tracker.success`. `Metric` only reports aggregates and does not alter any individual record’s success.

official_benchmark_assessment.description: The official evaluator computes task-completion status but does not score it, so released success does not separately require `supervisor.Task.status == "success"`. That is a real evaluator limitation, but it does not reach record-level different-outcome conflict here because all three retained successful runs also updated the task row to `status="success"` with `answer="null"`.

checklist_and_case_packet_assessment.description: The frozen checklist and case packet preserve exactly the five official registered tests, their conjunction, and the unscored status of `test.task_completed`; they do not add extra native or stronger conditions.

semantic_comparison.apparent_claim: This successful record appears to claim that Agent A solved the Venmo friend/unfriend task stated in `official/specs.json` for `c77c005_2`.
semantic_comparison.actual_checker: For this record, released success came from `records/agent_a/retained_record/native_evaluator_output.json::$.tracker.success`, i.e. all five registered tests passed; those tests did not separately score `test.task_completed`.
semantic_comparison.target_construction: The evaluator’s targets for this record were ground-truth answer `null`, added friendship IDs from `official/ground_truth/private_data.json::$.to_befriend_user_ids`, and removed friendship IDs from `official/ground_truth/private_data.json::$.to_unfriend_user_ids`.
semantic_comparison.aggregation: `runtime_wiring/official_appworld/evaluator.py::TestTracker.success` defines success as `pass_count == num_tests`; `runtime_wiring/our_system/appworld_official_worker.py::run_official_job` serialized that boolean and the released label remained `success`.
semantic_comparison.record_binding: `records/agent_a/retained_record/native_evaluator_input.json::$` and `records/agent_a/retained_record/run_summary.json::$` bind `task_id=c77c005_2`, `dataset_name=test_normal`, `experiment_name=appworld585_20260719_full_v1_agent_a_c77c005_2`; `records/agent_a/retained_record/appworld_task_output/version/code.txt::lines 1-1` and `records/agent_a/retained_record/appworld_task_output/version/data.txt::lines 1-1` bind code/data version; the retained end-state DB shows `status="success"`, `answer="null"`, and the matching friendship mutations.

our_system_review.summary: No issue found. The blind package stayed outcome-blind, the scorer relied on scorer-visible retained evidence plus frozen helper semantics, and the join mapped the same record’s `tracker.success` to the released label.
